[P3] Qualify stopping as occurring at an awaited checkpoint

Discarding a checkpoint does not necessarily stop the item. If an abandoned item finishes deserializing an already-checkpointed step and starts another default step, that step submits its START checkpoint without awaiting it. The checkpoint is dropped, but the new step's function still executes, potentially producing further side effects. Blocking occurs when it awaits a discarded checkpoint. Update this paragraph and the new `BatchItemStatus.STARTED` comment to say “next awaited checkpoint,” rather than promising that the next checkpoint stops execution.
